conviction_note: The fundamental read leans to a revenue beat. Consensus of $65.1M implies only +1.6% sequential growth, after Q2 grew 22% sequentially and last year's Q2-to-Q3 step was about 7%. The reaction read is close to balanced or slightly negative: the stock is +51% since the August print and above every sell-side target, the whisper is well above consensus, it has a +31.8 put skew and a 3.9 put/call OI ratio, and it sold two of its last three beat-and-raise prints. Hence print_vs_bar +4% against expected_move about -1, with abs_move kept at the option scale.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $65.1M and EPS -$0.10 consensus, with an EPS whisper of -$0.04 (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HTFL, fetched 2026-11-12). A Benzinga regional page in search snippets showed $65.2M (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/HTFL/earnings-forecasts, snippet only, 403 on fetch). FY2026 consensus is $248.63M (9 analysts, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/htfl/forecast/), the midpoint of the company's raised guide of $246-250M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001464521/000146452126000129/htfl-20260813xex99_1.htm, 2026-08-13). That guide implies H2 revenue of $129.3-133.3M against H1 of $116.7M. Implied Q4 consensus is about $66.8M. The bar is sourced to the company guide plus estimate sources within $0.1M of each other.
positioning_check: Short interest: no current figure reachable. MarketBeat and Nasdaq returned 403/503, and the only figure found was 1.11% of float with about 1.0 days to cover as of 2025-10-03 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/HTFL/short-interest, via search snippet), a year stale. There is no evidence of a crowded short. The tape: spot $59.70, 1.4% under the 52-week high, +191% off the low, +14.9% over 5 days and +17.3% over 20 days. The heavy put interest more likely reflects holders hedging a large run than shorts.

findings.finding: Q3 consensus revenue of $65.1M implies only +1.6% sequential growth over Q2's $64.1M. Q2 grew about 22% sequentially (Q1 $52.6M) and last year Q2-to-Q3 grew about 7% ($43.3M to $46.3M). Repeating last year's sequential step gives about $68.6M, a beat of about 5%. A beat of that size and carried through Q4 would lift FY above the $246-250M guide (implied ~$252M+), so a further raise is the likely line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise drew opposite reactions. Q3 2025 (2025-11-12): revenue $46.3M against about $42.0M estimate, a 10% beat, with a raise; stock -13.4%. Q1 2026 (2026-05-14): beat, guide raised $10M to $228-232M; stock -12.2%. Q2 2026 (2026-08-13): guide raised $18M to $246-250M, a raise larger than the beat; stock +35.7%. The stock pays only for a raise well above the beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits mechanically at the guide midpoint and is low on sequential growth. If the market had fully priced a large raise, the sell-side targets would sit above spot rather than about 15% below it, and the skew would not be +32 for puts. Against that, the +51% drift since August and an EPS whisper of -0.04 against -0.10 show a beat is widely expected, so only a raise beyond about $252-255M is likely to be new.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo conference summary (2026-09-09, https://quartr.com/events/heartflow-inc-htfl-wells-fargo-21st-annual-healthcare-conference_FVw2S7Ww): accelerating adoption, plaque coverage widening. Earnings Whispers whisper -0.04 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HTFL). The sequential arithmetic rests on the company's own 8-K figures.

findings.finding: At a 2026-09-09 conference, management said Plaque Analysis covered lives stood at 78% and should reach the mid-80s as Anthem and regional payers come online. It also said plaque ASPs are rising with coverage, a further contractual step-up is expected in early 2027, and plaque revenue should go from $1.5M last year to about $30M in 2026 (guide $29-31M, ~1,250 activated accounts). This supports an upbeat plaque line and 2027 commentary on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q2 the plaque guide was raised to $29-31M as part of the +35.7% beat-and-raise reaction. Plaque has not surprised separately on earlier prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It was a public conference comment, so it is largely priced. What is not yet known is whether Anthem coverage landed in Q3, since no Anthem policy was found in search, and how big the 2027 ASP step is. Plaque is about 12% of revenue (~$30M of ~$248M), so the rest of the company (FFRct, ~88%) has to hold its ~40% growth; this finding is sized net of that.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001464521/000146452126000129/htfl-20260813xex99_1.htm) calls plaque 'a meaningful second growth engine'. Quartr Q2 summary (https://quartr.com/events/heartflow-inc-htfl-q2-2026_FVw2SKlR) gives the $29-31M plaque guide and ~1,250 accounts. These are company sources and not independent of each other.

findings.finding: The CY2027 OPPS proposed rule set FFRct (CPT 75580) at $850.50 in APC 1510, down 3.1% from $877.34 in 2026, and kept plaque (75577) flat at $950.50. The final rule (2026-11-05/06) kept SaMS on New Technology APCs at rates close to 2026, effective 2027-01-01. This is a small Medicare price headwind on the core FFRct line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has turned on a CMS rate. The CY2025 CCTA payment increase was a tailwind cited by the company.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since July and finalised a week before the print, so mostly priced. It matters only if management quantifies a 2027 ASP impact on the call. Medicare hospital outpatient is only part of the payer mix, and the cut is 3%.
findings.independence: Reed Smith on the final rule (2026-11-06, https://www.reedsmith.com/our-insights/blogs/health-industry-washington-watch/102o8ks/cms-finalizes-interim-payment-policy-for-software-as-a-medical-service-in-hospita/): interim New Technology APC rates close to 2026. ACC summary (2026-11-05, https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/Articles/2026/11/05/14/15/CMS-Releases-Final-2027-Medicare-Physician-Fee-Schedule-and-Hospital-OPPS-Rules). The exact final 75580 rate was not confirmed.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is stretched. Spot is $59.70: +51% since the August print, +14.9% in 5 sessions (from $52.40 on Nov 6 after the TCT P4/NEJM and AHA DECIDE data of Nov 1-2), 1.4% under the 52-week high, and above the $50.5 average and near the $64 high sell-side target. The EPS whisper (-0.04) is well ahead of consensus (-0.10). The option market pays +31.8 vol points for 25d puts over calls with put/call OI at 3.9.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two of the last three beat-and-raise prints were sold by 12-13% (2025-11-12 -13.4%, 2026-05-14 -12.2%). The one bought (+35.7%) came off a much lower base, before the 51% drift.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The point is that the run-up has raised the bar above the published consensus. If the market were not positioned for a strong print, the stock would not sit above the targets of analysts who are 8 of 9 Buy, and the whisper would not be 60% ahead of consensus. The put skew agrees with this sign, so it is partly priced in the options, not in spot.
findings.independence: stockanalysis.com targets: average $50.5, high $64, 6 Strong Buy / 2 Buy / 1 Hold (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/htfl/forecast/). TCT/AHA data releases Nov 1-2 (https://finviz.com/news/413145/aha-2026-heartflow-plaque-analysis-associated-with-34-fewer-major-cvd-events-and-half-the-rate-of-heart-attack-at-one-year-in-prospective-decide-registry). Sealed baseline skew and run-up.

findings.finding: CEO John Farquhar sold 38,900 shares at $55.74 on 2026-11-10, two days before the print, including 15,620 shares from exercising $2.22 options. The sale was under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-09-12. On 2026-11-06, 7,751 shares were withheld for tax. Form 4/144 filings continued through Aug-Nov (21 Form 144s since August).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; routine plan sales have not moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public on EDGAR and the plan is pre-scheduled, so it carries almost no information. It is filed only because it is a dated insider sale inside the blackout run-up.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001464521.json) shows steady Form 144/4 flow since August.

findings.finding: Bain Capital Life Sciences, the IPO sponsor, sold about 4.0M shares in 2026 (2.0M on 2026-02-04 at ~$28.05, ~2.0M on 2026-04-28 to 30) and reportedly still holds about 8.45M shares (~9.8%). Selling came in the open windows after prints, so another sale or block after the print could weigh on the first session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The February sale came before a new 12-month low (2026-02-11 per MarketBeat headline); the April sales came about two weeks before the May print (-12.2%). No secondary block has been recorded on the day after a print.
findings.why_not_priced: The overhang is known. Whether Bain uses the post-print window, and at this price (2x its February sale), is not. A block would show as an overnight offering announcement. Sourced to aggregators; the underlying Form 4s were not read.
findings.independence: MarketBeat April 30 alerts (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/heartflow-nasdaqhtfl-major-shareholder-bain-capital-life-sciences-inv-sells-948757-shares-2026-04-30/). Same aggregator family, so not independent.

baseline_tension: The fundamental read (likely revenue beat and raise) cuts against the +31.8 put skew. The run-up and stretched positioning agree with the skew, so the net lean is slightly negative and p_up sits only 3 points under 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): this name sold two of three beat-and-raise prints by 12-13%, so the beat/raise finding was cut from +2.0 to +1.2 and p_up from 48 to 47.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): plaque is about 12% of revenue, so the plaque finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.5.

Lessons 6 and 7 left standing: the bar is sourced to the guide midpoint plus two estimate sources within $0.1M; the negative positioning finding agrees with the skew, and no crowded short was found to shrink it.
